articles.title: Adam Fantilli, Blue Jackets Agree to Massive Contract Extension, Details Revealed Before NHL Season
articles.summary: The Columbus Blue Jackets have resolved the contract dispute that led to center Adam Fantilli sitting out the start of training camp.
articles.body:
The Columbus Blue Jackets have resolved the contract dispute that led to center Adam Fantilli sitting out the start of training camp.

Fantilli and the Blue Jackets have agreed to a six-year, $13.75 million AAV extension that runs through the 2031-32 season, the team announced Thursday.

The new deal comes just one week before the Blue Jackets are set to open the regular season next Thursday against the visiting Buffalo Sabres.

Fantilli was selected by the Jackets with the third pick of the 2023 draft. He previously hit restricted free agency following the expiration of his three-year, $950,000 AAV entry-level contract.

Both players selected ahead of him in that draft also received massive extensions this offseason in the Chicago Blackhawks' Connor Bedard (five years, $15 million AAV) and Anaheim Ducks' Leo Carlsson (five years, $18 million AAV).

Fantilli is now playing on the NHL's fifth-highest cap hit this season behind Carlsson, Bedard, Kirill Kaprizov and Leon Draisaitl, per PuckPedia .

The center is heading into his age-22 season having recorded career highs in assists (35) and points (59) while playing all 82 games for a second straight season with the Jackets.

Those numbers made him the club's third most-productive player outside of Norris Trophy winner Zach Werenski and linemate Kirill Marchenko in a campaign during which the Blue Jackets made a push for a return to the playoffs before slumping down the stretch.

Locking Fantilli down on a new deal is especially important for the Blue Jackets when considering the uncertainty surrounding the futures of both Werenski and Marchenko.

The Blue Jackets included Werenski in a trade to the Dallas Stars that was ultimately vetoed by the player, per ESPN's Greg Wyshynski .

Both Werenski and general manager Don Waddell later released statements saying Werenski, who is currently signed through the 2027-28 season and becomes eligible for an extension next July, wanted to stay with the team.

Other questions surround the status of Marchenko, who is currently set to hit restricted free agency next offseason but whose agent has said doesn't plan to re-sign with the Jackets, per The Athletic's Aaron Portzline .

Marchenko did not provide definitive answers when asked last week if he wanted to be playing in Columbus.

Whether the Blue Jackets ultimately consider trading Marchenko ahead of the March 2027 deadline could depend on whether Waddell feels his team has a shot at the playoffs. Making sure Fantilli is available to serve as first-line center will be key to the Jackets' hopes of making their first postseason appearance in seven years.

articles.title: Why did Lindsey Vonn and Tiger Woods break up? The real reason behind their split as the skier goes public with new boyfriend
articles.summary: Lindsey Vonn and Tiger Woods were once one of the biggest sports couples in the world, bringing together two champions from very different sports.
articles.body: Lindsey Vonn and Tiger Woods were once one of the biggest sports couples in the world, bringing together two champions from very different sports. Their relationship began in 2013 and lasted for nearly three years before they announced their split in May 2015. More than a decade later, Vonn is back in the spotlight for her personal life after making her relationship with French alpine skier Matthieu Bailet public. The new romance has also brought fresh attention to one question fans have continued to ask: why did Vonn and Woods really break up? While stories over the years have suggested different possibilities, the two athletes gave a clear explanation when they ended their relationship, saying their demanding careers and the amount of time they spent apart had made the relationship difficult to maintain.Why did Lindsey Vonn and Tiger Woods break up?Vonn and Woods announced their breakup on May 3, 2015, after almost three years together, and both described the decision as mutual. Vonn explained that their lives had become incredibly hectic and that their careers forced them to spend much of their time apart. Woods shared almost the same explanation, saying that they were both competing in demanding sports and that finding enough time together had become difficult.At the time, their relationship had already shown how difficult it could be for two elite athletes to build a normal life together. Vonn’s career required her to travel around the world for alpine skiing competitions, while Woods had his own packed golf schedule, along with practice, tournaments and travel.They did make efforts to be part of each other’s lives. Woods travelled to Europe to support Vonn during major moments in her skiing career, while Vonn was regularly seen supporting Woods at golf events. Just weeks before their breakup announcement, she had even been with Woods and his children at the Masters Par 3 Contest.That makes their eventual split seem less like the result of one dramatic public incident and more like a relationship that became increasingly difficult to manage around two demanding careers.Was Tiger Woods or Lindsey Vonn’s career the reason behind the split?Based on what the two athletes themselves said publicly, neither person was blamed for the breakup. Vonn called the decision mutual, while Woods also described it as a mutual decision and spoke warmly about their relationship.Vonn said she would always cherish the memories they had created with Woods and that she would continue to admire and respect him. Woods also expressed admiration and love for Vonn, adding that she had been wonderful with his children, Sam and Charlie, as well as with his family.Their comments are important because they provide the clearest public record of why the relationship ended. Over the years, there have been stories and online speculation about other possible reasons, including claims about infidelity. However, neither Vonn nor Woods publicly confirmed that cheating was the reason for their breakup.In fact, their statements at the time pointed in a very different direction. Both athletes specifically talked about their schedules, the demands of their sports and the amount of time they were forced to spend apart. So while other theories have circulated since 2015, they should not be presented as established facts.The breakup was also emotionally difficult for Woods. Just days after the announcement, he described the period as “brutal” and said the situation was tough for him. (BBC⁠) That offered another indication that, despite the relationship ending, the split was not something he treated casually.Who is Lindsey Vonn’s new boyfriend Matthieu Bailet?More than 11 years after her split from Woods, Vonn has now made another athlete part of her public story. On September 23, 2026, the Olympic skier shared a series of vacation photographs on Instagram that included French alpine skier Matthieu Bailet, effectively confirming months of dating speculation. One of the pictures showed the pair kissing in a pool, while other photographs showed them enjoying time together near the water.Bailet, 30, is a French World Cup alpine skier who competes in downhill and super-G. The relationship had already attracted attention earlier in 2026 after Vonn and Bailet were spotted together in New York. At that stage, reports described them as getting to know each other, but neither had made the relationship fully public.That changed with Vonn’s latest Instagram post. She captioned the collection, “About that time for a summer recap… pt 1,” while Bailet also responded to the post and shared it on his own Instagram Stories.The relationship has naturally attracted attention because Bailet comes from the same world that made Vonn a global sports star. Unlike Woods, whose career is built around golf, Bailet understands the travel, training and pressure that come with professional alpine skiing. Whether that shared sporting background will shape their relationship is something only the couple can know, but it has certainly made their romance a major talking point among skiing fans.Is Matthieu Bailet Lindsey Vonn’s first relationship since Tiger Woods?No. Vonn had several important relationships after her time with Woods, so Bailet is not her first partner since their 2015 breakup.Vonn was previously engaged to former NHL player P.K. Subban. The pair announced their engagement in 2019 and later confirmed in 2020 that they had decided to end the engagement. She later dated business executive Diego Osorio, with Vonn confirming their separation in February 2025, according to reports.That makes her new relationship with Bailet another chapter in a long and very public personal journey. What stands out about the latest development, however, is that Vonn herself chose to share the relationship publicly after months of speculation.Her romance with Woods ended in 2015 with both athletes saying that their careers and constant time apart had made the relationship difficult. More than a decade later, Vonn is again dating a fellow sports figure, but this time the person beside her comes from the same skiing world she knows so well.For now, the clearest explanation for the Woods breakup remains the one both athletes gave at the time: their lives had become too demanding, they were spending too much time apart, and they mutually decided to move on while still expressing respect and affection for each other. The later rumors may continue to attract attention, but they do not change what Vonn and Woods actually said when they ended their relationship.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: California superintendent candidate ejected from sports league meeting for boisterous Title IX defense
articles.summary: Video shows Sonja Shaw confronting CIF Southern Section council members over transgender athletes in girls' sports before being removed from the meeting.
articles.body: California state superintendent candidate Sonja Shaw was removed from a California Interscholastic Federation Southern Section Council meeting Thursday after delivering an unscheduled speech demanding officials address transgender athlete participation in girls’ sports. Shaw, the president of the Chino Valley Unified School District Board of Education, told OutKick she was forced to leave the meeting in Long Beach after officials deemed her to be trespassing. Police were called, according to Shaw, but she said the responding officers were "very nice" and did not have to intervene. Video provided to OutKick showed Shaw standing before the council and challenging its members over the issue. CALIFORNIA GIRLS’ SPORTS ADVOCATES VOW FIGHT AFTER JUDGE TOSSES TRANS ATHLETE CASE: 'FAR FROM OVER' "I’m here on the front lines to protect our girls and their sports," Shaw said, interrupting the meeting. "I’ve never been able to address you guys as a body." The meeting’s published agenda included a public hearing session allowing speakers three minutes each. Shaw said during the confrontation that she arrived at 9:07 a.m. and had repeatedly asked CIF officials to place the participation of transgender athletes on a meeting agenda. "If you think it’s okay for a boy to play against our girls in sports, which is happening, you’re Southern Section. You are the representatives to stand up and do something," Shaw said. "You can fight back and stop using the state law. Federal supersedes state law." An official then called for a brief recess, but Shaw continued speaking. "How about any of you that are okay with this sit down? Any of you that want to fight the good fight and protect our girls, stand up," she said. "Are any of you okay? You guys are all okay with this?" As officials approached Shaw and repeatedly told her that she had to leave, she called on police to escort her from the room. "Call the cops, Mike. Let them escort me out," Shaw said. "No, you know it’s not right to let me get three minutes." Shaw continued challenging council members as she was ushered toward the exit and asked those who supported her position to stand. "So we have one guy in the room that’s willing to fight for our girls," Shaw said after one attendee apparently rose. She also accused the organization of ignoring pleas from female athletes who have contacted her for help. "We begged you to put it on the agenda. Why don’t you tell them the truth? How many times I asked you to put it on the agenda? You have the emails," Shaw said. "You guys are [a] CIF organization. You refuse to put it on the agenda and talk about it. … We have girls right now reaching out to me asking for help, and you’re sitting here acting like I’m some crazy lunatic because I’m interrupting a meeting. "I’m recording because I want people to see that you’re the representatives doing nothing," Shaw said before leaving. "I don’t care about losing votes. I don’t care about a seat. The point is, none of you are willing to do anything." INSIDE THE TRANS ATHLETE PODIUM CONTROVERSY SENDING POLITICAL SHOCKWAVES IN CALIFORNIA AHEAD OF ELECTIONS The incident unfolded amid an ongoing clash between California and the federal government over the state’s transgender athlete policies. California law says students must be permitted to participate in sex-segregated school programs and activities, including athletic teams and competitions, consistent with their gender identity. CIF’s gender-identity participation policy follows that requirement. The Trump administration has argued that the policy violates Title IX’s protections against sex discrimination. The Justice Department sued the California Department of Education and CIF in July 2025, alleging their rules deny female athletes equal opportunities by allowing biological males to compete in girls’ sports. California officials have defended their policies as consistent with state law. A federal judge dismissed the Justice Department’s lawsuit against the California Department of Education and CIF on Aug. 31. The court did not decide whether allowing transgender girls to compete in girls’ sports violates Title IX, instead ruling that California lacked clear notice that excluding transgender athletes was a condition of receiving federal education funding. The Justice Department said following the decision that it was evaluating a potential appeal. The issue received national attention when transgender athlete AB Hernandez competed in the girls’ division at the CIF state track and field championships. CIF introduced a pilot process allowing an additional biological female athlete to advance and receive a medal in events involving a transgender competitor, but critics, including Shaw, argued the accommodation did not resolve the underlying fairness issue. Shaw has made parental rights and protections for female athletes central parts of her political platform. She advanced from California’s June primary and is facing San Diego Unified School District board member Richard Barrera in November’s election for state superintendent of public instruction. articles.title: NHL sets its most confusing team history straight, and it's still pretty confusing
articles.summary: The NHL merged both Winnipeg Jets incarnations into one franchise history, creating quirks involving Teemu Selanne and Shane Doan's career records.
articles.body: The NHL has officially worked out one of its most confusing team histories by consolidating the histories of both incarnations of the Winnipeg Jets. While it clears some things up, it kind of makes it all a little bit more confusing. The Jets and the league announced on Wednesday that the statistical histories of both incarnations of the team have been merged. That sounds nice and simple... but it isn't. What's confusing is that the original Jets, which started in the World Hockey Association in the 1970s, were a different franchise than the one that plays in Manitoba today. The original team was one of four that merged into the NHL, but split for Arizona in 1996. Meanwhile, the Atlanta Thrashers debuted in 1999 and relocated to Winnipeg to become the current Jets. So, the OG Jets history actually belonged to the Coyotes, while the new Jets were the zombified remains of the Thrashers. Things got even more confusing when the Coyotes hockey assets were sold to what became the Utah Mammoth. However, Utah was treated as a new franchise, with the Coyotes and Jets history staying behind. If you need to take a break to splash some water on your face, go ahead because now it gets worse... With the OG Jets history merging with the current Jets/Thrashers record books, that leaves the Coyotes as their own franchise. This leads to some weird quirks. One is that Teemu Selanne's legendary rookie campaign during the 1992–93 season is now, statistically at least, tied to the Thrashers' history in a way. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! Meanwhile, Shane Doan was drafted by the Jets, played his rookie season in Winnipeg, and then played over 1,400 games for the Coyotes. Until now, in the record books, he only ever played for one franchise. Now, that fact is not totally accurate when you look through the record books. It also means that the late Dale Hawerchuk has become the current (and former) Jets' franchise leader in goals and points. Current Jet Mark Scheifele took those titles in 2025, and will need to do it again. However, he'll start the year seven goals and twenty-two points back from regaining the top spot. But the new way seems to be the best option... even if it's pretty head-scratching in its own right.

articles.title: Torrejón de Ardoz, ciudad de campeones y Patrimonio del Deporte de Radio MARCA
articles.standfirst: Jornada única en la ciudad madrileña con una programación especial de Radio MARCA y la Gala del Deporte de Torrejón de Ardoz
articles.summary: Jornada única en la ciudad madrileña con una programación especial de Radio MARCA y la Gala del Deporte de Torrejón de Ardoz
articles.body: Torrejón de Ardoz vivió una jornada para recordar con la llegada de la gira Patrimonio del Deporte de Radio MARCA. Coincidiendo con su condición de Ciudad Europea del Deporte 2026, la localidad madrileña se convirtió durante todo el día en la casa de la radio del deporte, con una programación especial y un reconocimiento a sus cuatro campeones del mundo: Jorge Garbajosa, Miriam Gutiérrez, Javi Limones e Iván Aurrecoechea, auténticos referentes de la historia deportiva de la ciudad madrileña. El gran colofón de la jornada fue la Gala del Deporte de Torrejón de Ardoz 2026, que reunió a destacadas figuras del deporte nacional y local y en la que fueron reconocidas, entre otras, las campeonas olímpicas María Pérez y Lydia Valentín, además de deportistas locales. Dentro de la jornada de Patrimonio del Deporte, Radio MARCA trasladó hasta Torrejón algunos de sus principales programas. La Pizarra, de 10:00 a 13:00 horas, y Directo MARCA, de 13:00 a 15:00, emitieron desde el Campus UCAM-COE, mientras que El Programa de Ortega, de 17:00 a 19:00 horas, tomó el relevo desde la Casa de la Cultura. Más de siete horas de radio en directo para acercar los micrófonos a los vecinos y convertir el deporte de Torrejón de Ardoz en protagonista. Uno de los grandes momentos de la jornada llegó con la entrega de los Premios Patrimonio del Deporte de Radio MARCA. Los reconocimientos fueron para Jorge Garbajosa, campeón del mundo de baloncesto; Miriam Gutiérrez, campeona del mundo de boxeo; Javi Limones, campeón del mundo de fútbol sala; e Iván Aurrecoechea, campeón del mundo de baloncesto 3x3. Cuatro nombres, cuatro disciplinas y cuatro campeones que representan el enorme patrimonio deportivo de Torrejón de Ardoz. El alcalde de Torrejón de Ardoz, Alejandro Navarro, acompañó a Radio MARCA durante una jornada especialmente significativa para una ciudad que en 2026 ostenta la distinción de Ciudad Europea del Deporte. Una celebración que sirvió para poner en valor a los deportistas de la localidad y el papel que el deporte desempeña en la identidad de Torrejón. La presidenta de la Fundación UCAM, María Dolores García Mascarell, también estuvo presente en la Universidad para explicar el gran proyecto educativo de UCAM-COE en Torrejón de Ardoz. Durante su intervención destacó la firme apuesta de UCAM por el deporte, una vinculación que la institución mantiene desde hace más de una década y que se ha convertido en uno de los pilares de su modelo educativo. Por la tarde llegó el gran colofón con la Gala del Deporte de Torrejón de Ardoz 2026, una auténtica fiesta que reunió a grandes nombres del deporte español junto a los principales protagonistas del deporte local. Entre las grandes premiadas estuvieron María Pérez y Lydia Valentín, dos campeonas olímpicas y referentes del deporte español. La gala tuvo además un momento especialmente significativo para la emisora. Radio MARCA recibió el premio a la comunicación deportiva por sus 25 años en las ondas, coincidiendo con la celebración de su cuarto de siglo contando las grandes historias y gestas del deporte español. Además, la Gala del Deporte de Torrejón de Ardoz reconoció a algunos de los grandes referentes y jóvenes talentos del deporte local. Los principales reconocimientos individuales recayeron en Iván Aurrecoechea, campeón del mundo de baloncesto 3x3, como mejor deportista masculino; las internacionales de fútbol sala Claudia Bollero y Alicia Voto, como mejores deportistas femeninas; y el exinternacional de baloncesto José Antonio Paraíso, premiado por su trayectoria deportiva. En las categorías colectivas fueron distinguidos Rivillos Academy Limones Juvenil, Torrejón Sala Alevín Femenino, Inter FS JP Financial y Club Voleibol Torrejón (UCAM Torrejón), mientras que el Club Ajedrez Torrejón recibió el reconocimiento a la mejor entidad deportiva.

articles.title: Portugal beat Wales 1-0 with Felix goal as Nations League defence begins
articles.summary: Joao Felix nets the only goal of the game, while Cristiano Ronaldo has an effort ruled out, as Portugal beat Wales 1-0.
articles.body:
Joao Felix scored the only goal with a long-range shot as reigning Nations League champions Portugal opened their campaign with a 1-0 home win over Wales.

Portugal, who have won two of the four finals since the competition was launched in 2018, dominated possession and outshot Wales 19-4 in Lisbon but squandered a string of chances.

Their only goal came after 22 minutes when a low scuffed shot by Felix from the edge of the box took a slight deflection off Wales captain Ben Davies and skipped inside the far post beyond Danny Ward’s desperate dive.

As it has for some two decades, Portugal’s attack revolved around Cristiano Ronaldo. Every time the 41-year-old, who made his national debut in 2003 and has since scored a record 146 international goals, touched the ball near the goal, the roar of the home crowd rose several octaves.

Ronaldo found the side netting once and shinned an inviting volley high over from close range. After an hour he slid the ball into the Wales net but, to his evident disbelief, was ruled offside.

He was still shaking his head when he was replaced seven minutes later.

The crowd grew quieter, and Portugal’s play drifted after Ronaldo’s departure.

Wales came agonisingly close to equalising, twice, from their one good chance.

First, Brennan Johnson chipped goalkeeper Diogo Costa and hit the face of the bar. With Costa stranded, Lewis Koumas and Dan James both went for the rebound. Koumas ended up shooting tamely straight at defender Ruben Dias on the line.

articles.title: Adam Fantilli agrees to 6-year, $82.5 million deal with Blue Jackets
articles.summary: After holding out the first week of training camp, Adam Fantilli, the Blue Jackets top young center, got a big raise and new contract with Columbus.
articles.body:
It took Adam Fantilli holding out for the first week of Blue Jackets training camp , but the team's top young center has agreed to a six-year contract worth $82.5 million ($13.75 million AAV) to finally put negotiations behind him and join his team at Nationwide Arena.

" Adam Fantilli has all of the tools you look for in a player ... speed, size, skill along with a competitive drive to succeed," Blue Jackets president/general manager Don Waddell said in a statement. "He is one of the most exciting young players in the NHL and a big part of what we are building in Columbus, so this is a very exciting day for our organization and our fans."

Fantilli, 21, became a restricted free agent without arbitration rights July 1. Had he signed a big offer sheet, like Anaheim Ducks center Leo Carlsson did with the Philadelphia Flyers , the Jackets would've been forced to match it or let Fantilli leave for a package of compensatory draft picks.

That didn't happen, allowing Waddell to seek a more team friendly cap hit than what Fantilli and agent Pat Brisson initially wanted. Getting their price, however, wound up costing Fantilli valuable preparation time with his teammates prior to opening the season against the Buffalo Sabres on Oct. 1 at Nationwide Arena.

NHL players who changed teams in the offseason

The Ducks weren't as fortunate from a cap perspective, swallowing hard before matching the Flyers' offer sheet that now pays Carlsson at $18 million a season for the next five years. Carlsson was selected second overall in 2023, one pick ahead of where the Blue Jackets got Fantilli , a comparable top young center who's similar in size, age and stats through their first three seasons .

According to PuckPedia , the Blue Jackets had just under $12.7 million in cap space prior to signing Fantilli, so they're about $1.2 million over the cap ceiling of $104 million for this season. That number, however, counts salaries for 14 forwards, seven defensemen and three goalies — including injured center Isac Lundestrom (Achilles surgery) and goalie Elvis Merzlikins (shoulder).

Merzlikins, who underwent shoulder surgery Aug. 17 , and Lundestrom will almost certainly start the season on IR, and both could be placed on long-term injured reserve to gain flexibility against the cap. Utilizing LTIR allows teams to exceed the cap ceiling by the amount that injured players placed on it puts them over. So, adding Merzlikins' $5.4 million and Lundestrom's $1.3 million salaries would provide plenty of cushion.

Teams are allowed to exceed the cap in the offseason by up to 10% of the ceiling, but must be cap compliant before 5 p.m. on Sept. 28.

Columbus Blue Jackets anchor lineup with Adam Fantilli contract

Fantilli is now the Blue Jackets' highest-paid player by a wide margin, exceeding the salary of reigning Norris Trophy winning defenseman Zach Werenski ($9.58 AAV) by roughly $4.1 million this season and next.

Though it doesn't come close to matching Carlsson's annual cap hit, Fantilli's salary now sits between Ducks power forward Cutter Gauthier 's new deal for $13.5 million over the next six years and Connor Bedard 's $15 million AAV for the next five with the Chicago Blackhawks .

Gauthier was selected fourth overall by the Flyers in 2022 and traded to the Ducks, while Bedard was the 2023 draft's first overall pick. Carlsson went second that year and Fantilli, whose numbers stack up comparably, went third. Fantilli has totaled 140 points on 67 goals and 73 assists through 213 games with the Blue Jackets, while Carlsson has give the Ducks 141 points on 61 goals and 80 assists and in 201 games.

Bedard tops both with 203 points on 75 goals and 128 assists in 219 games for the Blackhawks, but he's done it while posting a -98 plus/minus for a team that has lagged near the bottom of the NHL's overall standings.

Carlsson, who has a -1 plus/minus, helped the Ducks get back into the playoffs last season while Fantilli (-30) has narrowly missed the postseason the past two years with the Blue Jackets, a team that most analysts didn't consider a playoff contender.

Now, Fantilli is locked in with the Blue Jackets for six more years as an elite young center they'll need to continue improving over the course of this contract. Those type of gems are almost always drafted, rarely traded and almost never signed as free agents, which boosts their value immensely.

The NHL's best teams typically follow the same roster construct, starting with goaltending and defense before shifting to center ice. The Blue Jackets are doing well in those areas, especially after locking up Fantilli for a forward group that lost center Boone Jenner in free agency but has Sean Monahan , Charlie Coyle , Lundestrom and Cole Sillinger as additional center options.

articles.title: Steelers news: Does Joey Porter Jr. expect to play in 2026 amid stalled contract talks?
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have not made any progress with Joey Porter Jr. Pittsburgh is in a contract standoff with Porter that is bleeding into the regular se...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have not made any progress with Joey Porter Jr. Pittsburgh is in a contract standoff with Porter that is bleeding into the regular season. It is now an open question when the talented cornerback will play again, and if it will even be for the Steelers.

Porter gave some honest answers about his contract situation when talking to reporters on Thursday. He was asked how he felt after negotiations broke down before the regular season.

"It didn't get done, it didn't happen. That's really just old news for me now," Porter replied, per ESPN's Brooke Pryor. "It's mainly just focused on what I got ahead of me and really just getting back to 100%."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Porter also replied "yeah, definitely" when another reporter asked if he saw himself playing at some point this season.

That second answer does not look too surprising on the surface. But it could only mean a few different things given how much is happening around Porter right now.

Porter was back at practice on Wednesday though he only participated on a limited basis. He was officially listed with a non-injury/conditioning designation. Porter has been given the same injury designation in the past only to return to the injury report. That certainly matches the profile of a player in a contract dispute who does not want to practice without a new deal.

Pittsburgh is not actively shopping Porter , but that may be the best way to solve this problem. If the Steelers do not plan to extend Porter, keeping him sitting on the roster does little good. But there isn't much incentive for Pittsburgh to force a trade, especially in Aaron Rodgers' last season in the NFL .

It will be interesting to see how long it takes for Porter to action. Until then, Steelers fans should keep their eyes peeled for further developments.

Next up for the Steelers is a Week 3 matchup with the Bengals . This AFC North showdown kicks off at 1 p.m. ET on Sept. 27th from Acrisure Stadium.

articles.title: Rangers finish home slate with 3-1 win over Mets to keep Texas at least tied for AL West lead
articles.summary: Josh Jung and Corey Seager homered, Kumar Rocker pitched five solid innings and Texas closed out its home schedule with a 3-1 win over the New York Mets on T...
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Josh Jung and Corey Seager homered, Kumar Rocker pitched five solid innings and Texas closed out its home schedule with a 3-1 win over the New York Mets on Thursday that ensured that the Rangers would remain at least tied for the AL West lead heading into the regular season's final weekend.

Texas (79-80) stopped a three-game losing streak and moved a half-game ahead of Houston , which played Thursday night at the Athletics . The Astros (78-80) hold the head-to-head tiebreaker with the Rangers.

Texas, which finishes the regular season with three games in Minnesota , went ahead to stay on Jung's two-run homer in the first inning off rookie left-hander Zac Thornton (5-6). Seager snapped an 0-for-15 skid when he led off the sixth with his 19th homer.

Rocker (6-11) struck out four while allowing one run and three hits. Jordan Montgomery , the fourth Rangers reliever, worked a perfect ninth for his second big league save. He's made 161 starts and 17 relief appearances over nine big league seasons.

Francisco Lindor led off the game with a double and scored on Carson Benge's two-out single to put New York up 1-0. Benge has a Mets rookie record 160 hits.

Thornton struck out four and walked one in his five innings. He allowed four hits and the only runs he surrendered were on Jung's 12th homer. Seager went deep off Jefry Yan, another rookie.

Jung, who finished with three hits and a walk, is hitting .341 (15 for 44) in 11 games since coming off the injured list Sept. 12. He missed 47 games because of a left calf strain.

New York (73-86) goes to Washington (75-84) to open a three-game series Friday matching the two teams at the bottom of the NL East standings.

Texas plays Friday against the Twins, who never trailed while sweeping three games in Texas in mid-June.

articles.title: Why South Walton 2027 OL Alex Sansom picked Florida Atlantic football
articles.summary: Offensive lineman Alex Sansom, a key piece in South Walton's playoff hopes, has committed to his dream school in Florida Atlantic University.
articles.body:
Baker, South Walton and Walton football roll to wins

SANTA ROSA BEACH — Florida Atlantic University has long been Alex Sansom's dream school. A storybook official visit earlier in September cemented that for the South Walton offensive lineman, a three-star giant who last week committed to the 2-1 Owls.

After the Seahawks easily beat district foe Pensacola High, Sansom flew out at 5 a.m., arrived to Boca Raton and watched the Owls jump out to a 38-7 lead over Navy en route to their first win of the season. That was just the start to a perfect three-day visit.

"Since my sophomore year, I really loved FAU — loved the location, loved the weather, loved the school," Sansom said. "And when I found out that they wanted me to come on official visit, I was really excited. Being there and just seeing the culture of the school and the brotherhood, it was awesome. I got to go to into the locker room after the game and I saw everyone together and it really stood out to me how much it felt like home. Everybody treated me like family when I was there."

Standing 6-foot-4, 290 pounds, Sansom already looks the part of a collegiate lineman. So much so, he'll graduate early from South Walton and enroll early at FAU to get a jump on gelling with the program and acclimating to the next level.

"Coach (Stephen) Hamby, the offensive line coach, he said that he primarily wants me at center," Sansom said. "He's going to start me out at guard, but he wants to work me into the center role and teach me how to snap, things like that."

Sansom's parents have already sent one kid off to college (older brother is at TCU), and they supported the decision to leave home early for FAU.

"So my mom doesn't know much about football, but she was very excited and loved the school," Sansom said. "And my dad was just on cloud nine because we got to meet the head of the business school, and he's a big business guy. He just fell in love with the school and loves the football program, had a great time at the game. Across the board, it's really just a dream come true."

Sansom will major in business with the end goal of working in commercial real estate. But there's work to be done at South Walton, where Sansom was able to reunite this offseason with former IMG teammate JD Brown.

"I think I think we have a great team and we're really starting to click," Sansom said. "That Florida High loss was rough and we lost two really good linemen, but it's next man up and we always find a way to get through it. Our offense is starting to get into rhythm and we're moving the ball, bringing more energy to practice. So I feel like we're on track for a great season."

South Walton coach Phil Tisa is thankful to have Sansom's leadership on the line.

"Alex has been a great addition to our team," Tisa said, "and I couldn't be happier for him to have this opportunity at FAU."

articles.title: 79-80 – Rangers send off Shed with 3-1 win over Mets
articles.summary: The under.500 but first place Texas Rangers
articles.body:
The Texas Rangers scored three runs while the New York Mets scored one run.

After a couple of elsewise embarrassing defeats to the National League's New York squad to begin this crucial series, and with the threat of a crippling sweep, the Rangers decided to buckle down and give the hometown fans one last victory for the road in the final scheduled game at The Shed during this long, weird season.

To accomplish their victory, the Rangers turned to two of their biggest, most necessary catalysts at the plate and a cobbled together pitching staff working through things one pitch at a time.

Things started on an inauspicious note with today's starter Kumar Rocker allowing a first inning run that had to have had the faithful thinking, "the Rangers are really going to bookend the home slate with series sweeps at the hands of NL squads?"

Indeed, the first home series of the season for Texas was a sweep by the Cincinnati Reds and down 1-0 immediately, it was looking like the Mets had claimed favorable odds for pulling off a final ignominious sweep of Texas in their building even with the division still hanging in the balance.

Leave it to the guy who has been carrying the load since he returned to action to dissuade that notion as Josh Jung followed New York's first inning run with a two-run dinger in the bottom of the inning to put the Rangers up early. And, as we've learned over a whole summer and 80 home games, the Rangers having an early lead is perhaps the predominant key to their success.

To Rocker's credit, with the Rangers using the entire supply of duct tape in the state of Texas to try to hold their pitching staff together at the moment, the young right-hander stepped up and pitched five innings with the first inning run being his only blemish.

Overall Rocker went his five frames allowing the run on three hits and two walks while striking out four Mets. After Rocker left, the beleaguered bullpen was tasked with needing to wade through four innings in a one-run game. Texas got those four innings out of Robert Garcia, Tyler Alexander , Chase Silseth , and Jordan Montgomery with only Alexander allowing a base runner. Kudos to the 'pen. They stepped up today.

It didn't remain a one-run game either as Corey Seager finally came through after a rough series and gave the arms a bit of insurance with a solo home run in the bottom of the sixth. Eventually that allowed Montgomery to pick up the save with Jacob Latz unavailable. It was just the second save of Montgomery's career but it was a nice time to get it as Texas held on for the win.

With any luck, today's game won't actually be the final game played at The Shed this season but as far as the regular season goes, the Rangers are finished in Arlington. At 79-80, 14th best in baseball, the Rangers hold a half game lead over Houston for the American League West crown.

Player of the Game : We've taken to dubbing Jung "the straw" of late for being the straw that stirs the drink for what is a complicated offense that has been prone to disappear without him.

Today, without him, the Rangers and Met would presumably still be playing as his two-run home run in the bottom of the first to erase a 1-0 Mets lead proved the difference for a player who is proving to be a difference maker down the stretch.

Overall Jung went 3-for-3 with a walk to reach in each of his PAs today. Josh Jung wants some of that postseason action.

Up Next : The final series of the regular season begins for Texas as they travel up to Minnesota to take on a Twins squad that they have not beaten this year, as they were swept by them in Arlington back in June.

As the Rangers don't really have any starters left a starter has not been named for the opener. Meanwhile, Minnesota will opt for RHP Joe Ryan in the opener.

The Friday evening first pitch from Target Field is scheduled for 7:10 pm CDT and will be aired on the Rangers Sports Network.

articles.title: ‘It Was a Grind,’ Pirates’ Paul Skenes Reflects on Perplexing Season
articles.summary: PITTSBURGH – Paul Skenes’ perplexing 2026 season came to an end on Thursday afternoon at PNC Park. Skenes started against […]
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH – Paul Skenes ' perplexing 2026 season came to an end on Thursday afternoon at PNC Park.

Skenes started against the Cardinals in his team's final home game of the 2026 season. The right-hander held St. Louis to one run on three hits with two walks and eight strikeouts in a 2-1 Pirates' win , their 81st of the season.

"He threw the ball great," said manager Don Kelly .

Skenes was at 90 pitches with seven strikeouts through six innings, but he trotted out back to the mound for one more batter in the seventh inning. Skenes struck out Cardinals designated hitter Leo Bernal, which gave him 200 punchouts on the season. He became the third pitcher in Pirates history to have two consecutive seasons with at least 200 strikeouts.

"I was pushing to go back out," Skenes said of chasing his 200th strikeout. "I think if I had gotten a strikeout in the sixth there, I wouldn't have gone back out. But I basically asked for one hitter and [Kelly] gave it to me. I appreciate that."

Skenes entered the season with high expectations after emerging as perhaps the game's top starting pitcher. But the reigning National League Cy Young winner fell short of the heavy standard he set through his first two years with the Pirates. Skenes finished his third big-league big season 10-11 with a 3.82 ERA in 32 starts.

Despite an ERA jump of nearly two full points, Skenes feels like he still had a good – albeit challenging – season.

"It was a grind. It was definitely a grind," Skenes said of his season. "I think it was a good year. I don't think it was to the caliber of the last two years, but I'm not gonna sit around all offseason thinking about how bad this season was, because I just don't think that's true. I understand the standard that was set the last couple of years, but I think there was a lot of good and stuff to get better at. … but the thing that I'm happiest about is the 32 starts."

A disastrous first start of the year on Opening Day in New York was quickly erased by a dominant stretch through the middle of May. Back-to-back eight-inning outings capped off a stretch of nine starts in which Skenes combined for a 1.09 ERA. But beginning with his start against the Phillies on May 17, Skenes combined for a 4.56 ERA over his final 23 outings. The Pirates went 9-14 in those games.

From his time in college at LSU to a brief stint in the minor leagues before his two-year dominance in the big leagues, Skenes had never gone through the adversity that he endured this season. While the results weren't always the same as what they've been, Skenes' consistency remained in his off-the-field work through the challenges.

"We've talked a lot about nobody expects more from Paul Skenes than Paul Skenes expects from himself," Kelly said of his ace. "I know what everybody sees everyday is the same guy. Comes in, [is] focused, works his butt off. And it was tough for him going through that."

Now that his season is over Skenes, will take time to shift his focus towards 2027. Despite taking a step back this season, he still feels like better days are ahead. And given the improvement the Pirates have shown this year, he feels the same way about what lies ahead for his team.

"I think my best baseball is ahead of me and I think our best baseball is ahead of us. Got a long offseason and have the chance to sit down and look at all the stuff. It's really easy to get emotional and kind of let emotions bleed into some stuff during the season. To be able to sit back and kinda look at the big picture rather than the day-to-day, short-term view of it that takes over in-season, that will be good."

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo draws blank as Wales edged out by Portugal in Nations League
articles.summary: Portugal 1-0 Wales: Joao Felix’s deflected effort proved the difference for the hosts as Ronaldo had a second-half effort ruled out by VAR
articles.body:
Wales fell to an opening 1-0 Nations League defeat to Portugal as Cristiano Ronaldo drew a blank in Lisbon.

On an evening when Ronaldo missed a slew of chances and had a second-half effort ruled out by a VAR intervention, it was his Al Nassr team-mate Joao Felix who settled the contest.

Ronaldo was winning cap number 234 after deciding to prolong his international career following a disappointing World Cup, but his contribution ended when substituted after 67 minutes.

The manner of Felix's 22nd minute goal was cruel on Wales, deflecting off Ben Davies , but it could not be denied that Portugal deserved their victory by having 23 shots to five.

Being pitched into a tough Nations League A group with Portugal, Norway and Denmark was Wales' reward for promotion two years ago.

But boss Craig Bellamy – who was on the brink of leaving in the summer to join Burnley – had welcomed the challenge as an opportunity to improve their seeding for the 2028 European Championship.

Ronaldo was back at the Jose Alvalde Stadium, where he began his career with Sporting Lisbon , as the septuagenarian Jorge Jesus took charge for the first time.

On paper it looked a mismatch with Portugal ranked seventh in the world and 31 places higher than Wales, and their players drawn from major European clubs while Craig Bellamy's squad had been ravaged by injuries and withdrawals.

Key pair Harry Wilson and Joe Rodon were missing and the absence of goalkeeper Karl Darlow saw Wrexham 's Danny Ward make only his second appearance of the season.

The first half was a tale of Felix's strike and rising Ronaldo frustration.

Wales actually started in composed fashion, with Lewis Koumas occupying Portugal defenders and showing why he has impressed at Liverpool this season.

But Portugal gradually took control and Ronaldo fired wide from a tight angle before his poor touch allowed Neco Williams to recover.

Pedro Neto missed at the far post before Felix's 20-yard shot nicked off Davies to take the ball beyond Ward.

Ronaldo sent another opening wide before an untidy strike from 12 yards allowed Ward to collect, leaving the Portugal captain kicking the air in disgust.

The script stayed the same after the break as Ruben Neves set up a Ronaldo tap-in from four yards.

The wait for Ronaldo's 147th international goal seemed over, but his connection sent the ball sailing over to the bewilderment of home fans.

There was even more despair for Ronaldo when racing onto a Bruno Fernandes pass after 59 minutes.

Ronaldo slid the ball home and raced towards the corner flag for his trademark 'Siuuu' celebration, but VAR disallowed the goal for offside.

Wales almost produced an equaliser from nowhere as Brennan Johnson broke through and, from the byline, looped his effort on to the bar.

Koumas attempted to prod home the rebound but Ruben Dias made a superb clearance to deny Wales.

articles.title: Yo-Yo Ma joins Michigan band for ‘Lord of the Rings’ show
articles.summary: Yo-Yo Ma will join the Michigan Marching Band for a “Lord of the Rings”-themed halftime show Saturday at the Big House.
articles.body:
One does not simply walk into Michigan Stadium. But Yo-Yo Ma can apparently march into it with a cello.

The world-renowned cellist will join the Michigan Marching Band for a "Lord of the Rings"-themed halftime show Saturday, Sept. 26, when the University of Michigan takes on Iowa.

Presented as a collaboration between the University Musical Society (UMS) and the Michigan Marching Band, the performance marks the 25th anniversary of "The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring," the first film in Peter Jackson's blockbuster fantasy trilogy.

And while Wolverines fans may be more accustomed to hearing "The Victors" echo through the Big House than music from the Shire, Saturday's halftime show will bring several selections from Middle-earth to the field.

The program includes "Prologue: One Ring to Rule Them All," "Concerning Hobbits," "A Shortcut to Mushrooms," "Riders of Rohan" and "Isengard Unleashed."

Richard Frey, associate director of the Michigan Marching and Athletic Bands, and former Michigan Marching Band director Scott Boerma worked with "Lord of the Rings" composer Howard Shore to adapt the film score for marching band. Frey also arranged a cello cadenza for Ma.

"Collaborating with an artist of Yo-Yo Ma's extraordinary caliber is a transformative milestone for our student musicians," said John Pasquale, director of the Michigan Marching and Athletic Bands. "The Michigan Marching Band has a long legacy of musical excellence on the field, and sharing the stage — and gridiron — with Yo-Yo Ma elevates that tradition to unprecedented heights. It will be an unforgettable moment for the band, the stadium and everyone watching."

More than 100,000 fans are expected to be on hand for the unusual musical fellowship.

The Michigan Marching Band is no stranger to bringing movie scores onto the football field. Previous halftime shows have drawn from "Wicked," "Star Wars," James Bond, "Willy Wonka" and "Dune," as well as music by film composers John Williams and Hans Zimmer.

UMS also has a history of bringing some unexpected guests into the Big House. Actor Sir Patrick Stewart conducted the national anthem in 2006; the New York Philharmonic performed at halftime in 2015; and trumpeter Wynton Marsalis appeared with the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra for a 2022 halftime show .

For UMS, Ma's appearance also brings a longtime collaborator back into the fold.

"Yo-Yo Ma's relationship with UMS, the University of Michigan, and the Michigan community is truly singular," said Matthew VanBesien, president of UMS. "As we look ahead toward our 150th season, working closely in this partnership celebrates our shared past while pushing us into thrilling new artistic and civic territory. Bringing Yo-Yo onto the field at Michigan Stadium with the Michigan Marching Band is a powerful symbol of how music bridges disciplines, traditions, and communities."

Ma made his Ann Arbor debut in 1982 and has returned nearly 20 times since.

His Michigan adventures won't end when the last echoes of Isengard disappear from the Big House. Ma is scheduled to return Dec. 10 for a sold-out recital with his longtime collaborator, pianist Emanuel Ax, at Hill Auditorium.

Until then, there is one halftime show to rule them all.

BERLIN (AP) — Germany began a new era under Jürgen Klopp , Erling Haaland scored two goals for Norway , and Cristiano Ronaldo was still playing for Portugal in the Nations League on Thursday.

Klopp was all smiles in Amsterdam despite Cody Gakpo 's late equalizer for the Netherlands to draw 1-1 with Germany. Ruben van Bommel produced a brilliant cross that Gakpo met with a flying volley in the second minute of stoppage time.

The Netherlands was also making a fresh start under new coach Xavi Hernández , but it was a bruising game that always seemed capable of boiling over between two old rivals determined to arrest their slides from past heights.

Dutch players were unhappy when Felix Nmecha broke the deadlock in the 32nd because the Germans kept playing despite an injury to Brian Brobbey , who had to go off with what looked like a hamstring injury. Dutch captain Virgil van Dijk raised his finger and exchanged angry words with Jonathan Tah as the German celebrations prompted scuffles, whistles from the fans, and plastic cups thrown on the field.

There were more scuffles in the second half, especially after a bad challenge by Germany's Nadiem Amiri on Denzel Dumfries , who was able to continue. Dumfries later clashed with Germany captain Joshua Kimmich .

Amiri was only playing because Jamal Musiala suffered a thigh problem in the warmup. Kai Havertz also went off early after clutching the back of his left thigh.

In the other group game, Tasos Douvikas scored a last-second winner for Greece 2-1 in Serbia.

Haaland scored twice for Norway to beat Denmark 3-2 in Oslo to take his tally to 64 goals in 56 appearances for the country.

In the same group, the 41-year-old Ronaldo played 67 minutes for Portugal in a 1-0 win over Wales that gave new coach Jorge Jesus a successful start.

Jesus' decision to pair João Félix with the veteran star in attack paid off as the 26-year-old Félix's early strike from outside the penalty area was enough to decide the result.

Detroit Lions wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa has not been off to a good start this season. He has caught two passes for 26 yards and zero touchdowns on six targets, an average of 13.0 yards per reception.

With him not having much of an impact on the Lions offense, wide receivers coach Scottie Montgomery said Tuesday that TeSlaa's opportunities are going to stay limited because of how the offense is built. With this being the case, should the Lions trade him away? Could it potentially be for cornerback help?

Isaac TeSlaa Is The Lions' Biggest Trade Chip For A Cornerback

It is not a secret that Detroit needs to trade for a cornerback. In order to get something, sometimes things have to be given away. TeSlaa could be the best trade chip that general manager Brad Holmes has in his pocket. If he is not going to be used properly in this high-powered offense, then there are teams that could very well use another wide receiver.

TeSlaa has been on the field in both games this season and the stats do not have much to show for it. If he got an expanded role with the Lions or elsewhere, there is no doubt he has the potential to be a good option.

Tyson Campbell Of The Cleveland Browns Could Be An Option

The top name that has been floated around for the Lions to potentially acquire in a trade is Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr . Well, there is another cornerback that Detroit could potentially acquire on the trade market.

Mike Payton, a Lions writer for A to Z Sports , thinks that Tyson Campbell of the Cleveland Browns could be a potential trade option for the Lions. Payton said:

"Cleveland would be making this move because of roster construction. The Browns already have Denzel Ward on a huge deal. Campbell is also expensive going forward, and if their season falls apart, they could decide they don't need that much money tied up in two outside corners. TeSlaa gives them a cheap, young receiver with upside. This one is harder to pull off. Detroit would probably have to send TeSlaa plus something like a third-round pick because Campbell is only 26 and under contract through 2028. Campbell is the biggest upside swing of the three. He's 6-foot-1, athletic, and has experience playing press, man, and multiple zone coverages. articles.title: Last-gasp Gakpo strike snatches Dutch draw to sour Klopp debut
articles.summary: Cody Gakpo scored in stoppage time to snatch a 1-1 draw for the Netherlands at home to Germany on Jurgen Klopp's debut in the visiting dugout in the Nations...
articles.body:
Cody Gakpo scored in stoppage time to snatch a 1-1 draw for the Netherlands at home to Germany on Jurgen Klopp's debut in the visiting dugout in the Nations League on Thursday.

Germany led through a first-half strike from Felix Nmecha but Gakpo fired home a superb volley in the closing moments from a Ruben van Bommel cross.

The late equaliser was just rewards for the hosts who were aggressive and dominated much of the match under coach Xavi Hernandez, who was taking charge of the Netherlands for the first time.

"There's a long list of things that went well. We got off to a great start, then had real trouble for ten minutes," Klopp told Germany's RTL network.

"When the patterns of play aren't fully ingrained yet, you have to fight. I'm very pleased with many individual performances, and with the passion, too. But we can play better football -- most definitely."

Injuries to Jamal Musiala , who was scratched from the starting XI with a thigh complaint after the warm-up, and Kai Havertz , who left the field in the first half, could further sour things for Germany with three games remaining this international break.

"We wanted to be a nuisance, put them under pressure, and play high-energy football," said German debutant Philipp Treu .

"That worked really well, though we were too passive towards the end. But my god, the Dutch are a well-oiled machine."

Klopp took the reins after Germany's last-32 elimination by Paraguay at the summer's World Cup, their third straight early exit at a tournament they have won four times.

Used to taking over giants fallen on tough times, Klopp hoped to inject new blood into the side, bringing 16 debutants into the squad but named just one in the starting XI: defender Treu.

Also reeling from a disappointing last-32 World Cup exit, the hosts too turned to a big-name manager, with former Barcelona midfield strategist and Johan Cruyff disciple Xavi taking his first match in charge.

The Germans resembled an energetic Klopp side early on, but after 15 minutes Van Dijk headed in from a corner, only for the goal to be chalked off after a long VAR review.

Germany looked nervous as the hosts pressed, with goalie Marc Andre ter Stegen giving away possession cheaply and inviting danger in his first match since June 2025.

The Dutch continued to push the visitors back after the goal and had cause for complaint when Germany took the lead against the run of play with 32 minutes gone.

Netherlands Brian Brobbey went down injured in midfield but Germany played on, with Karim Adeyemi threading a pass for Nmecha to score.

Adeyemi had a golden chance to add a second but hammered over with the goal unguarded just before the break.

The hosts continued to lay siege to the German goal after the break. Mexx Meerdink scuffed the ball just wide with the goal beckoning on the 66th-minute mark.

With the visitors on course for an unlikely win deep into stoppage time, van Bommel burst down the left and curved a perfect cross over the defence and into the path of Gakpo, who fired home.

articles.title: Klopp delivers verdict on Germany debut after late Netherlands equaliser
articles.summary: Germany came painfully close to securing a win in Jürgen Klopp’s first match as head coach, but ultimately had to settle for a 1-1 draw against the Netherlan...
articles.body:
Germany came painfully close to securing a win in Jürgen Klopp's first match as head coach, but ultimately had to settle for a 1-1 draw against the Netherlands after Cody Gakpo scored a late equaliser.

Speaking after the game (via Focus.de), Klopp expressed his satisfaction with what he saw from his players, particularly their mentality, but also admitted there is room for improvement.

"I've stood on the touchline more than 1,000 times, so I know the position and that hasn't changed," Klopp said.

"I was very, very, very pleased with a lot of the individual performances. Overall, I was very happy with the passion we showed. We can play better and play more football, that's for sure.

"We created work for ourselves, which meant we had to run and put in the effort – it was demanding for both teams. I would have really loved to win, but I'm happy enough with the point."

Klopp and Germany will be back in action on Sunday when they face Greece.

articles.title: Giants bring back reliever Camilo Doval, who has a chance to make history
articles.summary: The San Francisco Giants claimed reliever Camilo Doval off waivers Thursday. If the former All-Star gets into one of their final three games as the 71st play...
articles.body:
The way the San Francisco Giants are going this year, there's no surprise when they add a new player to the ever-changing roster, but Thursday's move was a fun one.

Back with the team: reliever Camilo Doval , claimed on waivers from the Pirates. If the former All-Star closer gets into one of the team's final three games as the 71st player used, the Giants would tie the all-time big-league record.

San Francisco traded Doval, 29, to the Yankees last year for utility player Jesús Rodríguez, right-hander Trystan Vrieling , third baseman Parks Harber and left hander Carlos De La Rosa, and New York dealt Doval to the Pirates for two minor-leaguers Aug. 1.

Doval had a 3.79 ERA in 19 innings over 20 appearances with the Pirates and opponents hit .271 off him; he put up a 4.54 ERA in 44 outings with the Yankees this year. His main problem has come against left-handed hitters, who are batting .322 against him.

Doval spent his first four-plus seasons with San Francisco, earning 39 saves in 2023 and striking out 87 batters in 67⅔ innings. He's had only six save opportunities this season and saved one. He's arbitration-eligible, so the Giants could elect to keep him if they felt he might be a fit in the bullpen next year.

Doval is not the only possible player to add to the team's ongoing franchise record for most players used in a season: Catcher Zach Morgan is on the taxi squad and manager Tony Vitello would like to get him onto the roster and into a game before the end of the season. If both are used, San Francisco would hold the players-used record alone; Atlanta used 71 players in 2025.

"There's been a lot," Vitello said. "I don't think you're going to play a major-league season where there's not a lot. Everybody's story is a little bit different, but I think it's fair to say ours has been unique in a lot of different ways. That's a crazy scenario."

He added, tongue in cheek, "I guess you know, being first year in the organization, you'd like to get to meet everybody, so this is one way to do it."

Infielder Osleivis Basabe potentially could move to the IL with a leg injury and outfielder Bo Davidson left Wednesday's game after fouling a ball off the same area of his leg that cost him a week-plus of activity earlier this month, so there could be a Morgan sighting this weekend.

"Come hell or high water, I'd like to get him on that field and give him an opportunity to do something," Vitello said of Morgan, who's been up as an emergency option but never used. "We're kind of looking at scenarios and he did some fun things this year, swinging the bat and all the guys trust him behind the plate. If he is active, we'll get him on that field."

To make room for Doval on the 40-man roster, the Giants moved Blade Tidwell , diagnosed with a high-grade UCL sprain Tuesday, to the 60-day IL. San Francisco has a whopping 17 men on the 60-day IL, all of whom must be placed back on the 40-man roster after the season if the team plans to hold onto them - another reason to get a quick look at Doval and see if he might be in the 2027 plans.

Reliever Philip Abner , designated for assignment earlier in the week, was claimed by the Mets on Wednesday.

articles.title: Arsenal dealt injury blow as Kai Havertz limps off in Germany clash
articles.summary: Havertz was chosen to lead the line in Jurgen Klopp’s first match as Germany manager
articles.body:
Arsenal have been dealt an injury blow on the first night of the international break after Kai Havertz limped off during Germany's clash with the Netherlands .

Havertz was chosen to start by Jurgen Klopp for the former Liverpool manager's first outing in the Germany dugout, but his night was cut short after going down with what appeared to be a muscle problem.

After receiving treatment on his hamstring, which was heavily taped up, the forward was replaced by Younes Ebnoutalib on the half-hour mark.

It came minutes after Havertz was caught by a heavy challenge by Crystal Palace summer signing Quinten Timber on the knee, a foul the midfielder saw yellow for but could have realistically warranted a red.

Havertz spent much of the first half of last season sidelined with a knee injury, so Mikel Arteta will be praying that Havertz has not suffered any sort of recurrence with that issue.

Havertz was not the only injury casualty of the game that concerned a Premier League club, with Sunderland striker Brian Brobbey forced off with a hamstring issue.

The Dutch frontman came into the game off the back of his stunning hat-trick against Manchester City , taking home the match ball despite his side losing 5-3 at the Etihad Stadium.

However, he now faces a spell on the sidelines, pulling up and requiring help from the team doctor when leaving the field.

Brobbey was injured in the build-up to Germany's goal, which was scored in controversial fashion after it appeared Klopp's side were going to adhere to the Netherlands' request to stop play, only to continue and find the net through Felix Nmecha .

Jamal Musiala , meanwhile, was forced out of the match before the game even got underway despite being named in the starting XI, picking up a thigh problem in the warm-up. He was replaced by Nadiem Amiri .

articles.title: Joe Flacco sets record straight on if he expects to be traded to the Giants
articles.summary: Joe Flacco responds to questions about his future in Cincinnati
articles.body:
Is Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Flacco on the trading block?

Rumors began to swirl on social media that the New York Giants could be interested in trading for Flacco due to the recent injury to starting quarterback Jaxson Dart. Flacco has ties with Giants head coach John Harbaugh from their time together in Baltimore, where they won the Super Bowl in 2013.

The chatter on this subject has been loud enough that Flacco said his friends have made jokes to him about seeing him in New York soon. Flacco quickly put a stop to the conversation.

"It's obviously not real and not true," Flacco told The Enquirer." "But it was good enough to get people like certain friends of mine to get them to text me, 'hey, I'll see you in New York.' I was like, 'no, guys, you won't, that's not true.'"

Dart injured his knee Sept. 21 and will miss the rest of the regular season, Harbaugh told reporters. The Chicago Bears and Washington Commanders are also dealing with injuries to their starting quarterbacks.

It's highly unlikely the Bengals would be interested in trading Flacco. Cincinnati gave Flacco a lucrative deal for a backup position because of how much they value him. Flacco's contract is $6 million for one season and can go up to $9 million with incentives.

For the Bengals to shell out that much money for a player who doesn't even start, it shows how highly the organization thinks of him. The Bengals saw the importance of having a backup quarterback who can carry the offense and win games in 2025.

Joe Burrow injured his toe in the second week of the season last year, and former backup Jake Browning wasn't capable of orchestrating the offense at a high level. The Bengals knew to salvage the season they needed better play at the quarterback spot, and that's when the trade with the Cleveland Browns for Flacco happened.

The Bengals traded for Flacco on Oct. 7 last season. He went on to start six games for the team and gave the Bengals a chance to make the playoffs. The 41-year-old quarterback completed 251 of 416 passes for 2,479 yards and 15 touchdowns when Burrow was out.

Given Burrow's injury history, the organization has made it a point to remain ready for a worst-case scenario. Cincinnati feels it has a roster good enough to contend for a Super Bowl this season, and it's why keeping Flacco is necessary.

If Burrow were to suffer an injury and miss time, the franchise has full confidence in Flacco to lead the team.

So, although Flacco has heard the noise recently, he doesn't let it impact him.

"I just get a kick out of it," he said. "I haven't really given it too much thought at this point."

Flacco also understands the business aspect of the conversation. When he signed his contract to play for the Bengals, he relinquished control. The Bengals get to dictate when and where he plays for the remainder of the 2026 season, and there's no reason to believe it will be anywhere other than in Cincinnati.

"In these cases, it's not up to me," Flacco said. "I'm on the Cincinnati Bengals and because of that, that's my focus. Being here, doing the things that I need to do to get better each day while I'm here. Make sure I'm absorbing the game plan and all of those things. I get a little bit of a kick out of it, but it's kind out of my hands. I'm a Cincinnati Bengal, and I'm doing everything I can to get ready for the Pittsburgh Steelers."

articles.title: Paul Skenes Just Did Something Pirates Haven't Seen in 60 Years
articles.summary: Paul Skenes became the first Pirates pitcher in 60 years to accomplish a strikeout feat.
articles.body:
Though Paul Skenes will not win a second straight Cy Young, the Pirates ' ace has still turned things around in the second half of the season. He made some history before his regular season ended.

Skenes reached only 20.1 innings in August. In September, he exceeded that. He may have a 3.82 ERA compared to a 1.97 ERA last year, but his strikeout total has been impressive.

Against the Cardinals on Thursday, Skenes went 6.1 innings and struck out eight. He has over 200 strikeouts this year, striking out Leo Bernal to get the mark. Last year, he had 216.

Per Real App , Skenes is the first Pirates pitcher since 1966 to have consecutive 200-strikeout seasons.

Bob Veale went three straight years striking out 200+ batters. He had 250 strikeouts in 1964, 276 in 1965, and 229 in 1966.

Skenes has improved significantly since not lasting an inning against the Mets in March. Before the All-Star break, he won his first outing in ten starts. He's traded wins and losses, but Skenes believes there's a lot to be thankful for this year.

He will look back on his season and assess all aspects of his game, attempting to showcase a different Skenes next year.

"I learned a lot… From offseason to Spring Training, early in the season, stuff like that. I don't want to say everything's gone right my first two years, because I think you create your own luck, whatever the sayings are," Skenes said via MLB.com .

"I think in a lot of ways the pendulum has swung the other way this year. But in terms of controllables, I think I've learned a lot. When I show up at Spring Training next year, I'll have more of an answer. I'll have a lot of time to think about it."

articles.title: Jurgen Klopp denied debut Germany win as former player Cody Gakpo strikes late
articles.summary: Netherlands 1-1 Germany: Gakpo haunted his former Liverpool manager in stoppage time to cancel out Felix Nmecha’s controversial opener
articles.body:
Cody Gakpo denied his former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp a win in his first game in charge of Germany .

Felix Nmecha had put Germany ahead with what looked set to be the only goal of an intense Nations League match against the Netherlands at the Johan Cruyff Arena in Amsterdam.

But Gakpo scored a spectacular volley at the death to earn the Dutch a deserved point.

A controversial game saw Virgil van Dijk have a goal harshly disallowed while Germany's Kai Havertz and Dutch striker Brian Brobbey both suffered hamstring injuries .

Erling Haaland scored twice as Norway secured a 3-2 win over Denmark .

Oscar Bobb put the hosts ahead and Haaland doubled the lead with only 18 minutes on the clock.

Mikkel Damsgaard pulled one back for the Danes and Rasmus Hojlund equalised on the hour mark.

But Haaland grabbed a 74th-minute winner when he crashed home a first-time shot from a short corner.

Norway finished with 10 men after David Moller Wolfe was shown a second yellow card in stoppage time.

Cristiano Ronaldo had a goal disallowed in Portugal 's 1-0 win over Wales.

The 41-year-old thought he had tucked away career goal number 980 to double Portugal's lead, but a VAR check showed he was just offside.

The hosts had to settle for Joao Felix 's 22nd-minute strike despite a dominant display.

Israel's Sayed Abu Farchi was sent off for his celebration during a 3-1 defeat against Austria .

The Colorado Rapids forward was already on a yellow card when he equalised before picking up the corner flag and aiming it like a gun.

Austria, who led through Romano Schmid 's penalty, won it in stoppage time through goals from Phillipp Mwene and Sasa Kalajdzic .

Late goals from Christos Tzolis and Anastasios Douvikas saw Greece snatch a 2-1 win in Serbia, who led through Andrija Zivkovic .

The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in Pristina thanks to a goal seven minutes from time from Vedat Muriqi .

Elsewhere. Lithuania won 2-0 in Liechtenstein and Andorra were beaten 2-1 at home to Malta.

articles.title: Panthers WRs Jalen Coker, Xavier Legette miss practice with injuries ahead of Week 3 game vs. Browns
articles.summary: Two of Carolina's top three wide receivers did not practice on Thursday ahead of the Panthers' Week 3 game against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday.  Jalen Cok...
articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. (AP) — Two of Carolina 's top three wide receivers did not practice on Thursday ahead of the Panthers ' Week 3 game against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday.

Jalen Coker (ankle) and Xavier Legette (knee) were both non-participants after both practiced on Wednesday.

Coker battled through an ankle injury last week but was able to play on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons , hauling in eight passes for 66 yards in a 34-3 win. Coker, who has been one of the big surprises in the NFL so far this season with 16 catches for 204 yards receiving and two touchdowns, had practiced on a limited basis on Wednesday before being held out.

Legette, who had a 55-yard catch against the Falcons, was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

Panthers coach Dave Canales doesn't address reporters on Thursdays, so there was no immediate update on their availability from the team. Canales is expected address the situation on Friday when the Panthers release their game day injury designations.

The injuries would leave the league's second-highest scoring offense thin at wide receiver if both are out.

John Metchie and Brycen Tremayne are next in line to play, although David Moore could be promoted from the practice squad. Moore has spent several seasons under Canales and knows the offense well.

Carolina also added wide receiver Ihmir Smith-Marsette to the practice squad and he's a candidate to be active and return punts this week. Smith-Marsette spent time with the Panthers in 2023, although he was not a major contributor on offense.
